Wrote the reader output to `/home/mara/cwe-bench/pipelines/stacking/out/reader-ds/h4-12733.json`.

What I verified in the pinned tree and what the file records:

**Protections (4):** the `execute_sql` keyword gate with per-statement splitting (`src/tools/execute-sql.ts:26-29,58-63`), the custom-tool gate without splitting (`src/tools/custom-tool-handler.ts:186`), a per-execution `ExecuteOptions.readonly` declared but implemented by no connector (`src/connectors/interface.ts:62-71`), and a connection-level `ConnectorConfig.readonly` that only PostgreSQL/SQLite honour and that the TOML loader cannot set (`src/config/toml-loader.ts:628-634`).

**Key confirmed facts:** `grep` shows no connector references `options.readonly` at all; `config.readonly` appears only at `postgres/index.ts:176` and `sqlite/index.ts:192`. MariaDB is a separate class, not shared with MySQL. Both MySQL and MariaDB enable `multipleStatements` (`mysql:54`, `mariadb:53`), so their gate/tokenizer divergence reaches the engine. `scanSingleLineComment` treats `--` as a comment unconditionally (`sql-parser.ts:15-20`). SQLite allows the `pragma` keyword outright (`allowed-keywords.ts:13`) while the connector classifies only four pragma substrings as reads (`sqlite/index.ts:464-472`).

**11 traps in 8 independent groups**, with per-model tiers, five distinct dismissal arguments, two fix conflicts (connection-wide read-only vs. writable tools on one source; reject-all-pragma vs. the pinned `PRAGMA table_info` test), and seven fairness risks drawn from pinned tests.

**Verdict: usable.** Proposed design: postgres execution-layer backstop, mariadb as a separate implementation, sqlite backstop, sqlite PRAGMA coupling, and the MySQL/MariaDB `--` tokenizer — all sites the published fix touches, all gradeable without a SQL Server instance. SQL Server (`T5`, the strongest "absent plus reason to dismiss" trap) is recorded and recommended as an injected add-on only.

**Unverified** (kept out of the claims): the fix commit itself (not present at HEAD), READ ONLY transaction behaviour for `EXPLAIN`, SQL Server reachability, and the 16-hunk count.
